property_summary: For every bytes4 interfaceId input, the correct contract returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI.interfaceId when queried (i.e. supportsInterface(type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId) == true), but the mutant that removed that branch will return false for that interfaceId and thus violate this property for that input.

For every bytes4 input i, the reference contract returns true when queried with the IERC1155MetadataURI interface id (type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId) but the mutant that removed that branch will return false for that specific interface id; thus for any fuzzed bytes4 i equal to that interface id the reference returns true while the mutant returns false.

For any interfaceId the contract reports support for IERC1155 (type(IERC1155).interfaceId) exactly as the reference: supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) must return true; the mutant that removed that check will return false for that id and thus violate the rule for that input.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract reports support for IERC1155.interfaceId iff supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) returns true (i.e. the contract must return true for the IERC1155 interface id); the mutant removed that check so for that specific interface id the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C reports supportsInterface(interfaceId) == true whenever interfaceId equals IERC1155.interfaceId or IERC1155MetadataURI.interfaceId (or other supported ids), while the mutant specifically returns false for IERC1155.interfaceId — so the property is that supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) always returns true; the mutant breaks this for that interface id.

For every bytes4 interfaceId the reference C returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI.interfaceId if and also returns true for IERC1155.interfaceId when queried; the mutant removed the IERC1155 check so there exists an interfaceId (specifically type(IERC1155).interfaceId) for which the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.
For every bytes4 interface id equal to the ERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId), C.supportsInterface must return true; the mutant removed that check so it can return false for that id.

For any interfaceId input, the reference contract returns true from supportsInterface iff the id equals IERC1155 OR equals IERC1155MetadataURI (or is supported by super); the mutant wrongly returns true only if the id equals BOTH IERC1155 AND IERC1155MetadataURI at the same time, so there exist ids (e.g. IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI) where the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true whenever interfaceId equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI (or super); the mutant wrongly requires interfaceId to equal both simultaneously, so some interfaceIds (e.g. each individual IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI id) make the reference return true while the mutant returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true whenever interfaceId equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI (or is supported by super); the mutant incorrectly requires the id to equal both simultaneously, so some interfaceIds (e.g. exactly IERC1155 or exactly IERC1155MetadataURI) make the reference return true but the mutant return false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true whenever interfaceId equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI (or is supported by super); the mutant incorrectly requires the id to equal both at once, so there exist interfaceIds (e.g. exactly IERC1155 or exactly IERC1155MetadataURI) where the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true whenever the id equals IERC1155 OR equals IERC1155MetadataURI (or is supported by super); the mutant incorrectly requires the id to equal BOTH simultaneously, so some interfaceIds (e.g. each individual IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI id) make the reference return true while the mutant returns false.

For any non-zero account and any token id, balanceOf(account,id) must never revert and must equal the stored balance; the mutant removes the zero-address check so calling balanceOf(address(0), id) may return 0 instead of reverting (the reference reverts for the zero address), causing a behavioral difference.

For every address account and token id, balanceOf(account,id) on the correct contract returns the stored balance (no revert for non-zero addresses); the mutant erroneously reverts for all non-zero addresses and thus only succeeds for the zero address, breaking that property for many inputs.

For every account and token id, calling balanceOf(account,id) on the correct contract never reverts (and for account == address(0) it would revert in reference but the reference ensures the call either reverts for zero address or otherwise returns a uint); the mutant removes the zero-address require causing balanceOf(address(0), id) to succeed returning 0 — so the universal rule: calling balanceOf(account,id) either reverts iff account == address(0) (reference) but the mutant allows it to succeed for that input, violating the rule.

For every address `acct` and token id `id`, calling balanceOf(acct,id) on the correct contract either reverts when acct == address(0) and otherwise returns a uint; the mutant violates this by allowing balanceOf(address(0), id) to return (not revert) — so the property: calling balanceOf returns successfully iff acct != address(0).

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch returns each element equal to balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant instead uses ids[0] for every position, so when ids contains at least two different values and the corresponding balances differ the mutant will return a different array.

For any accounts[] and ids[] of equal length, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids)[i] equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i; the mutant instead uses ids[0] for every i, so when ids has differing entries and balances differ the mutant returns a different array.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids)[i] == balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i; the mutant incorrectly uses ids[0] for every position so this equality can be violated when ids contains differing ids whose per-account balances differ.
